frames.text: SECTIONAL VIEW THROUGH THE 35-TON TANK, MARK VIII

frames.name: p011-text-1000
frames.text: The Mark VIII machine is an armored track-laying type of fight-

frames.name: p011-text-1001
frames.text: ing tank in which the hull or body acts as the structural frame of the

frames.name: p011-text-1002
frames.text: tractor, as well as the housing for the propelling and fighting units

frames.name: p011-text-1003
frames.text: and crews. It differs from previous and other types of tractors and

frames.name: p011-text-1004
frames.text: self-propelling land units in that it has no chassis or supporting frame

frames.name: p011-text-1005
frames.text: structure, but more closely resembles marine structure, in that the

frames.name: p011-text-1006
frames.text: hull carries with it the entire mechanism and all of the running gear

frames.name: p011-text-1007
frames.text: except the track links which pass around the hull in the form of a

frames.name: p011-text-1008
frames.text: continuous belt on each side of the machine.

frames.name: p011-text-1009
frames.text: Propulsion on the Mark VIII machine is secured by taking the

frames.name: p011-text-1010
frames.text: drive from a 12-cylinder Liberty engine through a planetary gear

frames.name: p011-text-1011
frames.text: box, thence through a chain drive, which in turn actuates the driving

frames.name: p011-text-1012
frames.text: sprocket of the track. As the track is propelled continuously around

frames.name: p011-text-1013
frames.text: the machine, it carries with it sections of the rail over which the

frames.name: p011-text-1014
frames.text: rollers, upon which the machine runs, travel. The length of the track

frames.name: p011-text-1015
frames.text: belt allows the machine to accommodate itself to inequalities of the

frames.name: p011-text-1016
frames.text: ground, while at the same time providing a rail surface for the

frames.name: p011-text-1018
frames.text: The machine is 34 feet 2½ inches in length, 12 feet in width, and

frames.name: p011-text-1019
frames.text: the over-all height is 10 feet 3 inches. The engine and driving

frames.name: p011-text-1020
frames.text: members, including the clutch, the epicyclic transmission and chain

frames.name: p011-text-1021
frames.text: drive, are located in the rear of the hull. The engine together with

frames.name: p011-text-1022
frames.text: the clutch and epicyclic gearing and other necessary engine parts

frames.name: p011-text-1023
frames.text: occupy the engine room, which is 9 feet 9 inches in length.

frames.name: p011-text-1025
frames.text: From the rear of the engine room back to the center of the track-

frames.name: p011-text-1026
frames.text: driving wheel is 4 feet 8⅛ inches. In front of the engine room is

frames.name: p011-text-1027
frames.text: the fighting and operating room, at the forward end of which is the

frames.name: p011-text-1028
frames.text: driver’s seat with the control levers. On either side of the fighting

frames.name: p011-text-1029
frames.text: compartment there is a sponson or projecting swinging structure

frames.name: p011-text-1030
frames.text: carrying a 6-pounder gun. The sponsons contain gun mountings

frames.name: p011-text-1031
frames.text: capable of giving a wide radius of fire with the 6-pound guns. In

frames.name: p011-text-1032
frames.text: addition, the sponsons themselves may be swung back into the

frames.name: p012-text-1088
frames.text: interior of the fighting compartment to reduce the width of the

frames.name: p012-text-1089
frames.text: machine to permit it to be loaded on a standard railway car.

frames.name: p012-text-1090
frames.text: Surmounted above the fighting compartment is the main turret

frames.name: p012-text-1091
frames.text: which carries five machine guns. Above the main turret is the

frames.name: p012-text-1092
frames.text: directing officer’s coning tower from which it is possible to obtain

frames.name: p012-text-1093
frames.text: vision on all sides of the machine and from which its movements may

frames.name: p012-text-1094
frames.text: be directed. Located in the fighting compartment are sufficient

frames.name: p012-text-1095
frames.text: ammunition storage provisions for both 6-pounder and machine guns.

frames.name: p012-text-1096
frames.text: Entrance to the fighting compartment is secured through a door on

frames.name: p012-text-1097
frames.text: either side and in the doors there are also mounted machine guns.

frames.name: p012-text-1098
frames.text: This gives a total of seven machine guns, five being in the main

frames.name: p012-text-1099
frames.text: turret and two in the doors; and two 6-pounders, one located in each

frames.name: p012-text-1101
frames.text: The fighting compartment is separated from the engine room by a

frames.name: p012-text-1102
frames.text: bulkhead in which there are sliding doors.

frames.name: p012-text-1103
frames.text: The exterior portion of the hull is elongated on each side to provide

frames.name: p012-text-1104
frames.text: a guide for the track. The rear extremity contains the chain housing

frames.name: p012-text-1105
frames.text: for the chain drive and the track driving sprocket and the forward

frames.name: p012-text-1106
frames.text: extremity carries the track adjusting wheel which can be moved for-

frames.name: p012-text-1107
frames.text: ward or backward to tighten or loosen the track chain.

frames.name: p013-text-1119
frames.text: Steering is accomplished by allowing the track on one side to move

frames.name: p013-text-1120
frames.text: at a faster rate than the track on the other which tends to swing

frames.name: p013-text-1121
frames.text: the machine in the direction of the slow-moving track. If one track

frames.name: p013-text-1122
frames.text: is locked and the other track is moving ahead, the machine will

frames.name: p013-text-1123
frames.text: be turned in the narrowest possible radius. The radius in which

frames.name: p013-text-1124
frames.text: the machine can be turned depends to a large extent upon the nature

frames.name: p013-text-1125
frames.text: of the ground, as owing to its weight, it will dig up the ground to

frames.name: p013-text-1126
frames.text: the side as it is being turned, which will impede the rate at which

frames.name: p013-text-1127
frames.text: it can be swung around and will sometimes necessitate a wider

frames.name: p013-text-1130
frames.text: The units employed in propelling the Mark VIII machine are the

frames.name: p013-text-1131
frames.text: engine, which is the source of power; the clutch which connects

frames.name: p013-text-1132
frames.text: the source of power with the reduction gearing; an epicyclic or

frames.name: p013-text-1133
frames.text: planetary gear box which contains the reduction gear; a chain drive

frames.name: p014-text-1145
frames.text: which transmits the drive from the reduction gearing to the roller

frames.name: p014-text-1146
frames.text: sprocket; the roller sprocket and finally the track driving sprocket

frames.name: p014-text-1147
frames.text: which measures with the track links and propels the track. The

frames.name: p014-text-1148
frames.text: epicyclic gear box provides two speeds which may be utilized either

frames.name: p014-text-1151
frames.text: Control of the engine, clutch, epicyclic gear, reduction, steering,

frames.name: p014-text-1152
frames.text: etc., are all taken care of from the driver’s seat, which is located in

frames.name: p014-text-1153
frames.text: the forward end of the hull. The driver’s seat is of such a height

frames.name: p014-text-1154
frames.text: that the driver’s head is within a boxlike structure at the front

frames.name: p014-text-1155
frames.text: end of the main turret. There are slits cut in this compartment

frames.name: p014-text-1156
frames.text: which allow the driver to look to either side or ahead. The slits

frames.name: p014-text-1157
frames.text: can be closed by rotating protecting shields when under fire, and

frames.name: p014-text-1158
frames.text: when not under fire, the driver can raise a hinged door at the front

frames.name: p014-text-1159
frames.text: of the turret, allowing a clear and unobstructed view ahead of the

frames.name: p014-text-1161
frames.text: Outside of the spark and throttle connections and other engine

frames.name: p014-text-1162
frames.text: controls, the driver has four levers and a peddle. The two inside

frames.name: p014-text-1163
frames.text: levers are for shifting gears and control the epicyclic transmission.

frames.name: p014-text-1164
frames.text: The left outside lever controls the clutch and the right outside lever

frames.name: p014-text-1165
frames.text: is for reversing the peddle which is in the center of the track brake.

frames.name: p014-text-1166
frames.text: When either shifting lever is in neutral, the track brake on that aside

frames.name: p014-text-1167
frames.text: can be applied so that shifting both levers to neutral permits apply-

frames.name: p014-text-1168
frames.text: ing track brake to both tracks.

frames.name: p014-text-1171
frames.text: Before running, thoroughly clean all parts coated with grease or

frames.name: p014-text-1172
frames.text: slush applied for protection in shipment.

frames.name: p014-text-1173
frames.text: Fill radiator and water tanks with clear water.

frames.name: p014-text-1176
frames.text: THREE-QUARTER FRONT VIEW OF MARK VIII MACHINE

frames.name: p015-text-1178
frames.text: Fill oil reservoir of epicyclic transmission.

frames.name: p015-text-1179
frames.text: Lubricate entire machine in accordance with instructions. (See

frames.name: p015-text-1181
frames.text: Unpack and place all tools and equipment in proper locations.

frames.name: p015-text-1182
frames.text: (See Nomenclature List, pages 184 to 239, and other parts of book

frames.name: p015-text-1183
frames.text: dealing with specific tools and equipment.)

frames.name: p015-text-1184
frames.text: Important Note.—Before attempting to drive the Mark VIII

frames.name: p015-text-1185
frames.text: machine, be certain that the brake on the cardan shift is adjusted,

frames.name: p015-text-1186
frames.text: so that in shifting, the spinning of the shaft will be stopped or serious

frames.name: p015-text-1187
frames.text: damage to the transmission will occur.

frames.name: p015-text-1189
frames.text: To drive the machine, the following routine should be observed:

frames.name: p015-text-1190
frames.text: 1. Follow instructions on pages 51 to 61 regarding putting the

frames.name: p015-text-1192
frames.text: 2. Make sure that reversing lever is in neutral and clutch in full

frames.name: p015-text-1194
frames.text: 3. Start engine as per directions on page 51.

frames.name: p015-text-1195
frames.text: 4. Allow engine to warm up so that the temperature of the cooling

frames.name: p015-text-1196
frames.text: water in radiator is at least 160 degrees.

frames.name: p015-text-1197
frames.text: 5. Make sure epicyclic levers are in neutral.

frames.name: p015-text-1198
frames.text: 6. Pull back clutch lever all the way.

frames.name: p015-text-1199
frames.text: 7. Put reverse lever into forward position carefully and slowly.

frames.name: p015-text-1201
frames.text: 9. Let epicyclic lever into low speed (outside slots) and machine

frames.name: p015-text-1203
frames.text: 10. Shift either left or right lever to high speed, leaving clutch

frames.name: p015-text-1204
frames.text: engaged. (See page 150.) This will cause machine to swing in a

frames.name: p015-text-1205
frames.text: long arc due to difference in speed of tracks, but it is an easy way of

frames.name: p015-text-1206
frames.text: taking up the increased load due to shifting into high gear.

frames.name: p015-text-1207
frames.text: 11. Shift other lever to high gear.

frames.name: p015-text-1209
frames.text: To shift to low gear it is only necessary to move the levers into

frames.name: p015-text-1210
frames.text: low gear position without touching clutch.

frames.name: p015-text-1212
frames.text: 1. Put both shifting levers in neutral.

frames.name: p015-text-1213
frames.text: 2. Pull clutch lever back as far as it will go.

frames.name: p015-text-1214
frames.text: 3. When sure that cardan shift has stopped running, shift to reverse

frames.name: p015-text-1215
frames.text: by putting reverse lever in position (as shown on page 151).

frames.name: p015-text-1219
frames.text: To turn, put track on side toward which it is desired to turn into

frames.name: p015-text-1220
frames.text: neutral. If machine does not turn quickly, but moves ahead, de-

frames.name: p015-text-1222
frames.text: The pedal brake is interconnected with the transmission, so that

frames.name: p015-text-1223
frames.text: the brake can only be applied on the side which is in neutral.

frames.name: p016-text-1225
frames.text: The pedal is a positive brake on the track which is in neutral; it

frames.name: p016-text-1226
frames.text: does not effect a track when it is in low or high gear. Placing the

frames.name: p016-text-1227
frames.text: lever in neutral allows the brake on that side to be applied when pres-

frames.name: p016-text-1228
frames.text: sure is applied to the pedal.

frames.name: p016-text-1230
frames.text: To make a wide turn, the track on the side toward which it is

frames.name: p016-text-1231
frames.text: desired to turn should be in low gear, while the other track should

frames.name: p016-text-1232
frames.text: be in high gear. This allows the track on one side to turn at a faster

frames.name: p016-text-1233
frames.text: rate than that on the other and will give the wide turning arc desired.

frames.name: p016-text-1235
frames.text: In going over all obstructions which are sufficiently high to lift the

frames.name: p016-text-1236
frames.text: front end of the machine clear of the ground, the speed levers should

frames.name: p016-text-1237
frames.text: be slipped to allow the machine to ease itself over the obstructions.

frames.name: p016-text-1238
frames.text: It will be remembered that the weight of this machine is about 40

frames.name: p016-text-1239
frames.text: tons and it has to be allowed to gently absorb the shock due to its

frames.name: p016-text-1240
frames.text: returning to normal position after having been lifted clear of the

frames.name: p016-text-1241
frames.text: ground. By allowing the speed levers to slip the machine will grad-

frames.name: p016-text-1242
frames.text: ually come back into contact with the ground and the jar and shock

frames.name: p016-text-1243
frames.text: which would otherwise result can be avoided.

frames.name: p016-text-1245
frames.text: DRIVER’S SEAT AND CONTROLS, ALSO SHOWING AMMUNITION STORAGE

frames.name: p017-text-1248
frames.text: To accommodate the Mark VIII machine to the ordinary railway

frames.name: p017-text-1249
frames.text: transportation methods, it is possible to swing the sponsons in front

frames.name: p017-text-1250
frames.text: by the methods told on page 37. When the sponsons are swung in as

frames.name: p017-text-1251
frames.text: thus described and the guns in the sponsons are drawn back, the

frames.name: p017-text-1252
frames.text: standard railway flat car can be used.

frames.name: p017-text-1254
frames.text: It is estimated that the machine will consume 30 gallons per hour

frames.name: p017-text-1255
frames.text: of travel. At the speed of 5 miles per hour, this would mean one-

frames.name: p017-text-1256
frames.text: sixth of a mile per gallon, or with a capacity of 240 gallons, this would

frames.name: p017-text-1257
frames.text: mean a cruising time of eight hours or a cruising range of about 40

frames.name: p017-text-1258
frames.text: miles, estimating that the machine consumes 6 gallons per mile.

frames.name: p017-text-1259
frames.text: This, however, is only an estimate, and will vary in practice.

frames.name: p017-text-1261
frames.text: The lubrication of the Mark VIII machine is highly important, and

frames.name: p017-text-1262
frames.text: the performance of the machine depends largely upon how well the

frames.name: p017-text-1263
frames.text: following instructions are carried out. They should be made a matter

frames.name: p017-text-1264
frames.text: of routine, and followed exactly as laid down herewith.

frames.name: p017-text-1266
frames.text: The engine is lubricated from a reservoir on the starboard side of

frames.name: p017-text-1267
frames.text: the hull alongside the engine. Although the capacity of this tank

frames.name: p017-text-1268
frames.text: fitted on the machine is 16 gallons, not more than 4 or 5 gallons of

frames.name: p018-text-1271
frames.text: Liberty engine oil (see page 54) should be put in. If more than that

frames.name: p018-text-1272
frames.text: is put in, the tank is apt to flood the engine. This tank oils all parts

frames.name: p018-text-1273
frames.text: of the engine except one oil cup at the thrust bearing. This cup

frames.name: p018-text-1276
frames.text: The lower road track rollers are lubricated by removing the plugs on

frames.name: p018-text-1277
frames.text: the ends of the roller shafts. These rollers should receive a squirt

frames.name: p018-text-1278
frames.text: from the oil can once or twice a week, and the oil used should

frames.name: p018-text-1281
frames.text: The upper road track rollers are lubricated by removing the plugs

frames.name: p018-text-1282
frames.text: on the ends of the roller shafts, and filling as full as possible once or

frames.name: p018-text-1283
frames.text: twice a week with oil corresponding to the 600-W grade.

frames.name: p018-text-1285
frames.text: Be sure that the cups on each side of the epicyclic gear case, into

frames.name: p018-text-1286
frames.text: which passes the lead for the main bearings, is kept full of wool waste.

frames.name: p018-text-1287
frames.text: This allows of the gradual feed to the main bearings. No other

frames.name: p018-text-1288
frames.text: packing material should be placed in these cups, as the results will

frames.name: p018-text-1290
frames.text: The epicyclic gear is lubricated from the oil tank on the starboard

frames.name: p018-text-1291
frames.text: side of the hull, above the removable side plate. This oil tank is

frames.name: p018-text-1292
frames.text: filled through the plugs in the top, and has a capacity of 2 gallons of

frames.name: p018-text-1293
frames.text: 600-W oil. The tank should be inspected weekly, and filled to the

frames.name: p019-text-1296
frames.text: top. The oil is carried from the tank by a mechanical lubricator,

frames.name: p019-text-1297
frames.text: which oils the four main bearings, and the roller pinion shaft.

frames.name: p019-text-1298
frames.text: There is a cap on the top of the bevel gear case which should be

frames.name: p019-text-1299
frames.text: filled once a week, having a capacity of 2 gallons. This takes care

frames.name: p019-text-1300
frames.text: of the bevel gears and the shifter clutch, which governs the forward

frames.name: p019-text-1302
frames.text: The epicylic gear trains are taken care of by removing the two

frames.name: p019-text-1303
frames.text: caps or plugs in the gear case, and filling once a week with 3 gallons

frames.name: p019-text-1304
frames.text: of oil. To flush out the gear case, which revolves, the cap is first

frames.name: p019-text-1305
frames.text: brought to the top, and the gear case filled with kerosene and then

frames.name: p019-text-1306
frames.text: allowed to rotate to the bottom for draining. The case can then be

frames.name: p019-text-1307
frames.text: brought back so that the cap is at the top, and can be refilled by

frames.name: p019-text-1308
frames.text: putting 3 gallons of oil in each of the oil holes.

frames.name: p019-text-1310
frames.text: The front control rods are lubricated through the oil holes in the

frames.name: p019-text-1311
frames.text: lever shaft. Each of these holes should be given a squirt from the

frames.name: p019-text-1312
frames.text: oil can at least once a month.

frames.name: p020-text-1317
frames.text: To lubricate the center control rods it is necessary to remove the

frames.name: p020-text-1318
frames.text: center section of the ammunition rack. This can be lifted out, as

frames.name: p020-text-1319
frames.text: it is separated from the rack itself. The lubrication of the center

frames.name: p021-text-0002
frames.text: control rods is taken care of by oil holes on the top of each unit, and

frames.name: p021-text-0003
frames.text: these should receive a squirt from the oil can monthly.

frames.name: p022-text-0010
frames.text: The rear control rods should receive a drop of oil weekly on the

frames.name: p022-text-0011
frames.text: pins and on the wearing points.

frames.name: p022-text-0013
frames.text: The pins which connect the track links should receive an oil bath

frames.name: p022-text-0014
frames.text: in assembly. The track should be run through an oil bath monthly

frames.name: p022-text-0015
frames.text: by driving the machine through a prepared oil pool, or by swabbing

frames.name: p022-text-0016
frames.text: at accessible points, such as the mudholes.

frames.name: p022-text-0018
frames.text: The Sirocco cooling fan is lubricated through the oil plugs. There

frames.name: p022-text-0019
frames.text: is one plug on the fan casing and the other plug on the fan shaft.

frames.name: p022-text-0020
frames.text: These should receive a squirt from the oil can weekly.

frames.name: p022-text-0022
frames.text: The ventilating fan is lubricated by removing the oil plugs on the

frames.name: p022-text-0023
frames.text: ventilating-fan casing. Each of these holes should receive a squirt

frames.name: p023-text-0029
frames.text: The road track driving wheel is lubricated by removable plates on

frames.name: p023-text-0030
frames.text: the ends of the ventilating-fan driving-wheel shafts. They are on

frames.name: p023-text-0031
frames.text: the outside of the machine. The oil can should be applied to put as

frames.name: p023-text-0032
frames.text: much oil of the equivalent of 600-W as possible into the boss. This

frames.name: p023-text-0035
frames.text: The road track adjusting wheel is oiled through the plugs on the

frames.name: p023-text-0036
frames.text: ends of the road track adjusting-wheel shafts. The plugs are re-

frames.name: p023-text-0037
frames.text: moved, and by means of a squirt can as much 600-W oil as possible is

frames.name: p023-text-0038
frames.text: introduced. This should be done weekly.

frames.name: p023-text-0040
frames.text: Before attempting to adjust the track the threads of the road track

frames.name: p023-text-0041
frames.text: adjusting screw should be cleaned and thoroughly oiled. This

frames.name: p023-text-0042
frames.text: should be done whenever the track is adjusted.

frames.name: p024-text-0047
frames.text: The sprocket drive chain should be lubricated through the holes in

frames.name: p024-text-0048
frames.text: the links. It should also be well lubricated before assembly. This

frames.name: p024-text-0049
frames.text: should be taken care of daily if the machine is in service.

frames.name: p024-text-0051
frames.text: The roller pinions are lubricated through the holes in their cir-

frames.name: p024-text-0052
frames.text: cumference. To reach this remove the end hull plate on the side.

frames.name: p024-text-0053
frames.text: This should receive a squirt of oil monthly.

frames.name: p024-text-0055
frames.text: The clutch has a shaft which holds the clutch-control links. The

frames.name: p024-text-0056
frames.text: oil holes in the links should receive a squirt from the oil can weekly.

frames.name: p024-text-0058
frames.text: The air pump should receive oil through the two plugs in the top of

frames.name: p024-text-0059
frames.text: the pump. About a cup full of oil is required for each of these plugs,

frames.name: p024-text-0060
frames.text: and they should be lubricated weekly.

frames.name: p024-text-0062
frames.text: The fan bevel box should contain about a quart of 600-W oil, or

frames.name: p024-text-0063
frames.text: equivalent, and should be filled monthly.

frames.name: p025-text-0067
frames.text: The jockey pulley is lubricated through the plug in the side of the

frames.name: p025-text-0068
frames.text: pulley, opposite the ball-bearing center. This should receive a squirt

frames.name: p025-text-0069
frames.text: from the oil can every week.

frames.name: p025-text-0071
frames.text: The generator has two oil plugs on the side, into each of which two

frames.name: p025-text-0072
frames.text: or three drops of light oil, such as Veedol light, should be placed,

frames.name: p025-text-0075
frames.text: There are two oil plugs on each end of the starting motor, into

frames.name: p025-text-0076
frames.text: which two or three drops of light Veedol oil should be placed, bi-

frames.name: p025-text-0079
frames.text: All accessible bearing parts of the clutch, with the exception of the

frames.name: p025-text-0080
frames.text: cone surface, should receive a squirt of oil from the can weekly.

frames.name: p025-text-0082
frames.text: Before placing the road track on the machine give the links a

frames.name: p025-text-0083
frames.text: thick coating of heavy oil, and also the drive-wheel teeth, in order to

frames.name: p025-text-0084
frames.text: reduce the wear on the links.

frames.name: p026-text-0089
frames.text: The sponson hinges and rollers should receive a few drops of oil

frames.name: p026-text-0090
frames.text: monthly, and before drawing in the sponson.

frames.name: p026-text-0092
frames.text: The following parts should be lubricated daily: Cup at engine

frames.name: p026-text-0094
frames.text: The following parts should be lubricated biweekly: Lower road

frames.name: p026-text-0096
frames.text: The following parts should be lubricated weekly: Epicyclic gear

frames.name: p026-text-0097
frames.text: tank; epicyclic gear trains; rear control rods; cooling fan; ventilating

frames.name: p026-text-0098
frames.text: fan; road track driving wheel; road track adjusting wheel; clutch

frames.name: p026-text-0099
frames.text: shaft; air pump; jockey pulley; clutch.

frames.name: p026-text-0100
frames.text: The following parts should be lubricated monthly: Cap on top of

frames.name: p026-text-0101
frames.text: bevel gear case; front control rods; center control rods; road track

frames.name: p026-text-0102
frames.text: pins; roller pinions; fan bevel box.

frames.name: p028-text-0112
frames.text: LAYOUT OF GASOLINE PRESSURE-FEED SYSTEM USED ON 35-TON TANK, MARK VIII

frames.name: p030-text-0180
frames.text: The gasoline or petrol supply is carried in three tanks, of 80 gallons

frames.name: p030-text-0181
frames.text: capacity each, mounted near the rear of the machine, just below the

frames.name: p030-text-0182
frames.text: top plating. The gasoline or petrol tanks are all similar, and are

frames.name: p030-text-0183
frames.text: mounted side by side. The gasoline is forced by pressure from these

frames.name: p030-text-0184
frames.text: three tanks to a gravity tank mounted directly above the engine,

frames.name: p030-text-0185
frames.text: from which the flow is by gravity and pressure to the two carburetors.

frames.name: p030-text-0186
frames.text: Pressure is supplied by the engine-driven air pump, the pump being

frames.name: p030-text-0219
frames.text: Valve bracket holder and gas inlet

frames.name: p031-text-0227
frames.text: a four-cylinder design, operated by the cam shaft. The gasoline

frames.name: p031-text-0228
frames.text: tanks are placed to the rear of the engine room and separated from

frames.name: p031-text-0229
frames.text: it by means of the bulkhead.

frames.name: p031-text-0231
frames.text: The air pump is mounted just above the clutch, and is driven by a

frames.name: p031-text-0232
frames.text: V belt on the pulley on the engine-shaft brake. The pulley on the

frames.name: p031-text-0233
frames.text: air pump operates the cam shaft, which works directly against the

frames.name: p031-text-0234
frames.text: pistons or plungers of the pump. Before the engine is in motion, a

frames.name: p031-text-0235
frames.text: sufficient pressure can be secured to start the flow of fuel by means

frames.name: p031-text-0236
frames.text: of a hand pump, located on the bulkhead between the engine room

frames.name: p031-text-0237
frames.text: and fighting compartment. The flow is received from one of these

frames.name: p031-text-0238
frames.text: three tanks, depending upon which one of the cocks is open to the

frames.name: p031-text-0239
frames.text: gravity tank, located above the engine. The triple combination tap

frames.name: p031-text-0240
frames.text: is a ground key cock type, with a T handle between the tank and

frames.name: p031-text-0241
frames.text: carburetor, and controls the flow from the individual tanks. The

frames.name: p031-text-0242
frames.text: type of connections used on the gasoline system are flexible metal

frames.name: p031-text-0243
frames.text: hose soldered into T union connections.

frames.name: p031-text-0245
frames.text: To fill the gasoline tank it is necessary to unlock the hinge plates

frames.name: p031-text-0246
frames.text: over the caps by means of a socket wrench key. These two hinged

frames.name: p031-text-0247
frames.text: plates are lifted up, and this exposes the three filler caps or inlets in

frames.name: p031-text-0248
frames.text: the top of the tank. These caps are removed, and the gasoline tanks

frames.name: p031-text-0251
frames.text: To start the gasoline flow it is necessary to use the hand pump.

frames.name: p032-text-0272
frames.text: The gasoline system has a pressure feed (see p. 28) with three

frames.name: p032-text-0273
frames.text: supply tanks in the rear end of the hull and a pressure regulating

frames.name: p032-text-0274
frames.text: tank over the engine. The air pressure is furnished by a piston air

frames.name: p032-text-0275
frames.text: pump, mounted on a frame over the cardan shaft, from which the

frames.name: p032-text-0276
frames.text: pump is operated by means of a belt. Three air tubes of ¼-inch

frames.name: p032-text-0277
frames.text: armored flexible brass tubing run from the pump to the roof of the

frames.name: p032-text-0278
frames.text: machine, where they are connected to tees from one end of which

frames.name: p032-text-0279
frames.text: tubing of the same type leads along the under side of the roof to ball

frames.name: p032-text-0280
frames.text: check valves which are connected to the lower valves of the com-

frames.name: p032-text-0281
frames.text: bination tap which passes through the bulkhead between the engine

frames.name: p032-text-0282
frames.text: room and gasoline-tank compartment. From the rear end of the

frames.name: p032-text-0283
frames.text: combination tap ½-inch tubes lead to the top of the three gasoline

frames.name: p032-text-0285
frames.text: From the forward ends of the tees ¼-inch outside diameter seam-

frames.name: p032-text-0286
frames.text: less copper tubing runs along the upper right-hand corner of the tank

frames.name: p032-text-0287
frames.text: to the bulkhead, where each is connected to a main tube of the same

frames.name: p032-text-0288
frames.text: which leads to a pressure hand pump mounted on the engine-room

frames.name: p032-text-0289
frames.text: bulkhead over the port engine-room door. On the engine-room bulk-

frames.name: p032-text-0290
frames.text: head are mounted air-pressure gauges, tubes from which are con-

frames.name: p032-text-0291
frames.text: nected with the tubes from the tanks to the hand pump. Between

frames.name: p032-text-0292
frames.text: the gauges and the main line to the pump are fitted ground spindle

frames.name: p032-text-0293
frames.text: valves with levers. From the remaining plug on the air-pressure

frames.name: p032-text-0294
frames.text: pump a ¼-inch flexible brass tube leads to the pressure-regulating

frames.name: p032-text-0295
frames.text: tank over the engine. Just before reaching the regulating tank it is

frames.name: p032-text-0296
frames.text: connected to a cross. From one side leads a ¼-inch copper tubing

frames.name: p032-text-0297
frames.text: which connects to a pressure gauge on the bulkhead showing the

frames.name: p032-text-0298
frames.text: pressure in the regulation tank. A pet cock is connected with the

frames.name: p032-text-0301
frames.text: From connections in the filling pipes of the gasoline tanks three

frames.name: p032-text-0302
frames.text: 5-inch flexible brass tubes (Titeflex) lead to three connections in the

frames.name: p032-text-0303
frames.text: rear end of the combination tap on the bulkhead. In the front end

frames.name: p032-text-0304
frames.text: of the tap are fitted three valves with nut heads. Connected to

frames.name: p032-text-0305
frames.text: these valves are ball check valves; from the ball check valves ¼-

frames.name: p032-text-0306
frames.text: inch tubing runs to the three way connection, from which a ½-inch

frames.name: p032-text-0307
frames.text: tube leads to the side of the regulating tank.

frames.name: p032-text-0308
frames.text: From underneath the regulating tank two ¼-inch tubes, with

frames.name: p032-text-0309
frames.text: ground spindle lever valves at the tank, lead to the forward and rear

frames.name: p033-text-0330
frames.text: Petrol tubes from tank to combination tap.

frames.name: p033-text-0333
frames.text: Air-pressure tubes tank to combination tap.

frames.name: p034-text-0338
frames.text: SIDE OF HULL WITH SPONSON AND GUN

frames.name: p035-text-0340
frames.text: The hull of the Mark VIII machine is composed of armor plate of

frames.name: p035-text-0341
frames.text: various thickness, ranging from 6 to 16 mm. (0.236 to 0.630 inch).

frames.name: p035-text-0342
frames.text: The side elevation of the hull is a modified ellipse, flattened along the

frames.name: p035-text-0352
frames.text: Thickness of backplates, rear of gasoline (petrol) tank

frames.name: p035-text-0364
frames.text: Thickness of main turret side plates

frames.name: p035-text-0367
frames.text: Thickness of main turret top plates

frames.name: p035-text-0373
frames.text: Thickness of hemispherical turrets in doors and main turret

frames.name: p035-text-0376
frames.text: Thickness of lookout turret plating, top

frames.name: p035-text-0397
frames.text: Thickness of sponson floor plates, forward

frames.name: p035-text-0400
frames.text: Thickness of sponson floor plates, aft

frames.name: p035-text-0403
frames.text: Thickness of roof plate abaft turret

frames.name: p035-text-0406
frames.text: Thickness of roof plate over engine

frames.name: p035-text-0409
frames.text: Thickness of roof plate over petrol, gasoline tank

frames.name: p035-text-0412
frames.text: Thickness of roof plate over driver

frames.name: p035-text-0418
frames.text: Length of main turret, over all

frames.name: p035-text-0421
frames.text: Width of main turret, over all

frames.name: p035-text-0424
frames.text: Height of main turret, without outlook turret

frames.name: p035-text-0436
frames.text: Height of lookout turret above main turret

frames.name: p036-text-0447
frames.text: bottom for length of contact between the track and the ground and

frames.name: p036-text-0448
frames.text: flattened along the top. From above, or in plan the hull appears

frames.name: p036-text-0449
frames.text: in H form, the cross bar of the H being the hull or body proper,

frames.name: p036-text-0450
frames.text: containing the engine and fighting compartments, while the uprights

frames.name: p036-text-0451
frames.text: of the H represent the side plates of the hull which also act as guides

frames.name: p036-text-0453
frames.text: Not only does the hull act as the container or housing for the

frames.name: p036-text-0454
frames.text: driving and fighting mechanism as well as the crew, but it is also the

frames.name: p036-text-0455
frames.text: backbone structure of the entire machine. The plating of the hull,

frames.name: p036-text-0456
frames.text: therefore, performs the three functions of acting as a housing, as a

frames.name: p036-text-0457
frames.text: protection and also as a supporting structure.

frames.name: p036-text-0459
frames.text: REAR END SHOWING TRIANGULAR SPLASH PLATE AND TOWING EYE

frames.name: p037-text-0461
frames.text: Within the sides of the hull and projecting from it are two sponsons

frames.name: p037-text-0462
frames.text: which carry 6-pounder guns. These sponsons are carried outboard to

frames.name: p037-text-0463
frames.text: allow the guns to have a forward range as well as covering a wide arc

frames.name: p037-text-0464
frames.text: on either side of the machine. They are located at the forward end

frames.name: p037-text-0465
frames.text: of the fighting compartment. The gun mounts are capable of ro-

frames.name: p037-text-0466
frames.text: tating in the sponsons to give the necessary flexibility of fire.

frames.name: p037-text-0467
frames.text: In order to accomodate the Mark VIII machine to the limitations

frames.name: p037-text-0468
frames.text: of railway transportation it is possible to draw the sponsons inboard.

frames.name: p038-text-0472
frames.text: This is accomplished by removing the bolts connecting the angle

frames.name: p038-text-0473
frames.text: bar flange with the hull shell plating at the rear end of the sponson.

frames.name: p038-text-0474
frames.text: Removing these bolts frees the sponson and allows it to be swung

frames.name: p038-text-0475
frames.text: back on a hinge bracketed to the forward extremity of the sponson

frames.name: p038-text-0476
frames.text: and to the shell plating at this point.

frames.name: p038-text-0477
frames.text: To further narrow the machine so that no part will project in ship-

frames.name: p038-text-0478
frames.text: ment by rail, beyond the 9-foot railway loading gauge, the guns in

frames.name: p038-text-0479
frames.text: the sponsons are drawn back. The machine-gun mounts which pro-

frames.name: p038-text-0480
frames.text: ject from the doors in the sides of the hull are also designed to just

frames.name: p038-text-0481
frames.text: equal, but not to exceed the 9-foot loading width.

frames.name: p038-text-0483
frames.text: Near the inner edge of the sponson in rear of the ammunition stow-

frames.name: p038-text-0484
frames.text: age is the sponson roller which carried the weight of the sponson

frames.name: p038-text-0485
frames.text: when being moved in or out.

frames.name: p038-text-0486
frames.text: The sponson roller bracket is bolted to the floor of the sponson

frames.name: p038-text-0487
frames.text: above the floor plate, and has a short bearing on each side for the

frames.name: p038-text-0488
frames.text: roller shaft. The roller is 40 mm. bore, 110 mm. outside diameter

frames.name: p038-text-0489
frames.text: and 27 mm. wide and runs on roller track for the sponson, which is

frames.name: p038-text-0490
frames.text: on an arc of a circle with the sponson hinges as a center. The track

frames.name: p038-text-0491
frames.text: is a steel bar ¾ inch wide by 4 inches high and is held by bolts to

frames.name: p038-text-0492
frames.text: three brackets which are riveted to the floor.

frames.name: p038-text-0494
frames.text: On the top of the hull there is located the main turret. This is

frames.name: p038-text-0495
frames.text: rectangular in form and carries surmounted upon it the lookout

frames.name: p038-text-0496
frames.text: turret which is also rectangular in form. At the forward end of the

frames.name: p038-text-0497
frames.text: main turret is located the driver’s turret, also of rectangular form.

frames.name: p038-text-0498
frames.text: The lookout turret is of such a height that when a man stands on the

frames.name: p038-text-0499
frames.text: officers’ kit box located on the ammunition storage compartment

frames.name: p038-text-0500
frames.text: below it, his head will be at the proper height to look out through

frames.name: p038-text-0501
frames.text: the peepholes on all sides of the machine.

frames.name: p038-text-0503
frames.text: PROGRESSIVE STEPS IN UNCOVERING REVOLVER HOLE

frames.name: p039-text-0506
frames.text: There are three main doors in the hull; two are in the fighting com-

frames.name: p039-text-0507
frames.text: partment, located on each side at the rear, and the other is at the top

frames.name: p039-text-0508
frames.text: of the machine entering into the main turret from above. The side

frames.name: p039-text-0509
frames.text: doors are 28½ inches wide and 41⅞ inches high. The top door is 20

frames.name: p039-text-0510
frames.text: inches along the length of the machine and 15⅞ inches wide. In

frames.name: p039-text-0511
frames.text: addition, there are other openings in the hull for observation or other

frames.name: p039-text-0512
frames.text: purposes. In the front end of the driver’s turret there is a plate

frames.name: p039-text-0513
frames.text: which can be swung outward, allowing the driver a clear vision for-

frames.name: p039-text-0514
frames.text: ward when not under heavy fire. Similarly there are openings on

frames.name: p039-text-0515
frames.text: each side of the main turret just forward of the lookout turret which

frames.name: p039-text-0516
frames.text: can be swung open to give a clear view on either side of the machine.

frames.name: p039-text-0517
frames.text: The side doors leading into the fighting compartment are pierced for

frames.name: p039-text-0518
frames.text: machine-gun mounts and there are also five holes in the main turret to

frames.name: p039-text-0519
frames.text: provide for five additional machine guns. The spherical mounts for

frames.name: p039-text-0520
frames.text: these machine guns fit into these holes.

frames.name: p040-text-0561
frames.text: The top of the hull is pierced at the rear end between the tracks

frames.name: p040-text-0562
frames.text: by openings for the intake and exhaust air louvers. These louvers

frames.name: p040-text-0563
frames.text: are above the engine-room compartment. The intake louver is

frames.name: p040-text-0564
frames.text: above the forward end of the engine at the front end of the engine

frames.name: p040-text-0565
frames.text: compartment and the exhaust louver is above the radiator at the rear

frames.name: p040-text-0566
frames.text: end of the engine compartment. The openings in which the louvers

frames.name: p040-text-0567
frames.text: are fitted are rectangular. The dimensions of the intake-louver

frames.name: p040-text-0568
frames.text: opening are 3 feet 1¼ inches wide by 2 feet 1.825 inches long and the

frames.name: p040-text-0569
frames.text: exhaust-louver opening is 3 feet 1¼ inches wide by 3 feet 1⅝ inches

frames.name: p040-text-0571
frames.text: The louvers are composed of bars of 6 mm. armor plate bent to an

frames.name: p040-text-0572
frames.text: angle of 90 degrees and spaced face to face in herringbone style,

frames.name: p040-text-0573
frames.text: so that while permitting the air to readily pass through they act as

frames.name: p040-text-0574
frames.text: a baffle against projectiles or fragments, causing them to lose their

frames.name: p040-text-0575
frames.text: energy before entering the engine compartment. The extreme width

frames.name: p040-text-0576
frames.text: of each louver blade, outside to outside, is 2½ inches. The radius

frames.name: p040-text-0577
frames.text: around which the blade is bent in turning to the 90-degree angle is

frames.name: p040-text-0578
frames.text: one-half inch. There are 29 blades in the outlet louver and 34 blades

frames.name: p040-text-0579
frames.text: in the inlet. The proper distance between the louvers is held by

frames.name: p040-text-0580
frames.text: 122 carbon steel distance pieces, which take care of both the inlet

frames.name: p040-text-0583
frames.text: SIDE OF TURRET SHOWING CAMOUFLAGE BRACKET
